company: PayNova (fictional Indian fintech: UPI payments + digital lending)

impact_model.note: Illustrative demo logic. Direct enforcement chain only - no guessing across unrelated controls, so it does not over-alert.
impact_model.policies: clause -[:MAPS_TO]-> policy   (if none and the clause SUPERSEDES an older clause, inherit the older clause's mapping = memory/precedent)
impact_model.systems: control -[:RUNS_ON]-> system, plus downstream system -[:DEPENDS_ON]-> system
impact_model.baseline: keyword search = non-clause nodes whose keywords overlap the clause's keywords (what a doc/vector search over the circular text finds)

scenarios.name: DPDP erasure clause lands (headline demo)
scenarios.story: Legal forwards a DPDP update on the right to erasure: 'who do we need to talk to?'

expected.explanation: Keyword search finds 2 documents that say 'erasure/deletion'. The graph walks the enforcement chain to the encryption control, both data stores, and the 3 owners who actually have to act - none of which mention 'erasure'.

scenarios.name: Amendment reuses precedent (memory)
scenarios.story: Two months later DPDP amends the erasure timeline to 30 days. Nobody has mapped the new clause yet.

expected.explanation: The new clause has no mapping of its own. It SUPERSEDES the old clause, so the agent inherits that mapping and returns the full impact instantly - every mapping the team confirms becomes precedent for the next circular.

scenarios.name: RBI grievance rule (scoped, no over-alert)
scenarios.story: RBI tweaks the grievance-redressal rule. Should NOT light up the whole company.

expected.explanation: Only the support workflow and its owner are affected. Security, data and lending teams are not paged.

scenarios.name: RBI APR disclosure (crosses into the data layer)
scenarios.story: RBI changes how all-in APR must be disclosed.

expected.explanation: The KFS generator never says 'APR' but enforces the same policy, and the lending engine depends on the user DB - a 2-hop system dependency keyword search can't see.
